#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Connect to GitHub or Bitbucket and verify access to the current repo.
# Usage: connect.sh <git|bitbucket>
# Exit codes: 0 connected, 2 not logged in (prints what to run), 3 logged in but no access to this repo.
set -euo pipefail

target="${1:?usage: connect.sh <git|bitbucket>}"
# Same remote rule as pr-summ/fetch_pr.sh: upstream (fork workflow) else origin.
remote="$(git remote get-url upstream 2>/dev/null || git remote get-url origin 2>/dev/null || true)"
slug="$(sed -E 's#^(git@|ssh://git@|https?://([^@/]+@)?)[^/:]+[:/]##; s#\.git$##' <<<"$remote")"
cfg="$HOME/.config/pr-agent/bitbucket.env"

case "$target" in
git|github)
  gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "NOT_CONNECTED: run 'gh auth login' (GitHub.com, HTTPS, login with browser)"; exit 2; }
  echo "OK: GitHub logged in as $(gh api user -q .login)"
  if [[ "$remote" == *github.com* ]]; then
    gh repo view "$slug" --json nameWithOwner -q '"OK: access to " + .nameWithOwner' 2>/dev/null ||
      { echo "NO_ACCESS: logged in, but this account can't read $slug"; exit 3; }
  else
    echo "NOTE: current folder is not a GitHub repo; cd into your project to verify repo access"
  fi
  ;;
bitbucket|bb)
  [[ -z "${BITBUCKET_[redacted] && -f "$cfg" ]] && source "$cfg"
  if [[ -z "${BITBUCKET_EMAIL:-}" || -z "${BITBUCKET_[redacted] ]]; then
    if [[ ! -t 0 ]]; then
      echo "NOT_CONNECTED: run this in your own terminal (it asks for email + API token):"
      echo "  bash $0 bitbucket"
      exit 2
    fi
    read -rp "Atlassian account email: " BITBUCKET_EMAIL
    read -rsp "Bitbucket API token (hidden): " BITBUCKET_TOKEN; echo
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$cfg")"
    (umask 077; printf 'BITBUCKET_EMAIL=%q\nBITBUCKET_[redacted] "$BITBUCKET_EMAIL" "$BITBUCKET_TOKEN" >"$cfg")
    echo "Saved to $cfg (only you can read it)"
  fi
  if [[ "$remote" == *bitbucket.org* ]]; then
    curl -sf -o /dev/null -u "$BITBUCKET_EMAIL:$BITBUCKET_TOKEN" \
      "https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/$slug/pullrequests?pagelen=1" ||
      { echo "NO_ACCESS: credentials rejected or token can't read PRs of $slug (needs read:repository + read:pullrequest scopes)"; exit 3; }
    echo "OK: Bitbucket access to $slug"
  else
    echo "OK: Bitbucket credentials saved; cd into a Bitbucket project to verify repo access"
  fi
  ;;
*)
  echo "usage: connect.sh <git|bitbucket>" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac

# pr-agent — Claude Code skills for PR summaries

Two [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) skills:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/pr-connect git` | Connect to GitHub and check access to the current project |
| `/pr-connect bitbucket` | Connect to Bitbucket Cloud and check access to the current project |
| `/pr-summ <number \| "description">` | Fetch a PR from the current project and write an editable Markdown commit summary |

Only PRs of the project you're in are fetched. The repo comes from its `upstream` remote (fork workflow) or else `origin`, and GitHub vs Bitbucket is detected from that URL.

Works in the **Claude Code CLI** and the **Claude desktop app (Code tab)**. It doesn't work in claude.ai chat, which has no local repo or logins.

## 1. Install

Tell Claude Code:

> Install the skills from https://github.com/Amanlabh/pr-agent: clone it to ~/.claude/pr-agent and symlink every folder in its skills/ into ~/.claude/skills/

or run it yourself:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Amanlabh/pr-agent ~/.claude/pr-agent
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && ln -s ~/.claude/pr-agent/skills/* ~/.claude/skills/
```

Restart Claude Code, then type `/pr-` and you should see `/pr-connect` and `/pr-summ`.
Update later with `git -C ~/.claude/pr-agent pull`.

**Requirements:** `git`, `jq`, `curl`, plus [`gh`](https://cli.github.com) for GitHub (`brew install gh`).

## 2. Connect

### GitHub
1. In Claude Code, `cd` into your project and run `/pr-connect git`.
2. If you're not logged in, type `! gh auth login` and choose **GitHub.com → HTTPS → Login with a web browser**.
3. Run `/pr-connect git` again. It should print `OK: GitHub logged in as <you>` and `OK: access to <owner/repo>`.

### Bitbucket Cloud
1. Create an API [redacted] → avatar → **Account settings → Security → Create API token with scopes** → app **Bitbucket** → scopes `read:repository:bitbucket` and `read:pullrequest:bitbucket`. Copy the token.
2. In **your own terminal** (not the chat), run:
   ```bash
   bash ~/.claude/skills/pr-connect/connect.sh bitbucket
   ```
   It asks for your Atlassian email and the token (input is hidden) and saves them to `~/.config/pr-agent/bitbucket.env`, readable only by you.
3. In Claude Code, inside your Bitbucket project, run `/pr-connect bitbucket`. It should print `OK: Bitbucket access to <workspace/repo>`.

Alternative: export `BITBUCKET_EMAIL` and `BITBUCKET_TOKEN` in your shell profile instead. Never paste tokens into the chat.

## 3. Use

From inside your project:

```
/pr-summ 42
/pr-summ "login timeout fix"
```

- Number → that PR. Description → searches PR titles (open, merged, declined). If several match, Claude asks which one.
- The summary is saved to `pr-summaries/<host>-PR-<n>.md` and shown in the chat. It covers the summary, grouped changes, commits, files touched, testing notes and a suggested squash commit.
- Edit the saved file freely. To change the format for every future summary, edit `skills/pr-summ/template.md`.

## Limits
- Bitbucket: only the first page is read (50 commits, 100 files).
- Bitbucket Server/Data Center isn't supported (it uses a different API).

The following skills are available for use with the Skill tool:

- pr-connect: Connect Claude to GitHub or Bitbucket so /pr-summ can read pull requests, and verify access to the current project. Use when the user says "connect github", "connect bitbucket", "set up bitbucket token", or invokes /pr-connect git or /pr-connect bitbucket.
- pr-summ: Fetch a pull request from GitHub or Bitbucket (auto-detected from the repo's origin remote) by PR number or short description, and write an editable, reusable commit summary in Markdown. Use when the user says "summarize PR 42", "PR summary for the login fix", "commit summary for this PR", or invokes /pr-summ.

The repo is public at **https://github.com/Amanlabh/pr-agent**, and both commands are installed on your machine.

**Test results:**
- **`/pr-summ`:** I ran `claude -p "/pr-summ 9000"` inside a clone of `cli/cli`. Claude fetched that PR and saved a full summary to `pr-summaries/github-PR-9000.md`, including grouped files, testing steps and a squash commit.
- **`/pr-connect git`:** logged in as Amanlabh and confirmed access to the repo.
- **Outside a git repo:** the fetch stops with "cd into your project first".
- **`/pr-connect bitbucket`:** I only tested the "not connected" path, where it correctly says to run the setup in your own terminal. I haven't tested it against a real Bitbucket account, because there's no token here.

**What changed:**
- **New `/pr-connect`:**
  - `/pr-connect git` checks your `gh` login and access to the current repo. If you aren't logged in, it tells you to run `! gh auth login`.
  - `/pr-connect bitbucket` checks your saved credentials and repo access. The first time, you run a short setup in your own terminal: it asks for your Atlassian email and API token and saves them in a file only you can read (`~/.config/pr-agent/bitbucket.env`). Tokens never go through the chat.
- **Only this project's PRs:** PRs are fetched only from the repo you're in. It uses the `upstream` remote if there is one (for forks), otherwise `origin`. The output now shows which repo it read.
- **README:** covers install, connecting GitHub, connecting Bitbucket (with token scopes), usage and limits.
- **New layout:** the repo now holds both commands, so installing is a clone plus a symlink:
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/Amanlabh/pr-agent ~/.claude/pr-agent
  mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && ln -s ~/.claude/pr-agent/skills/* ~/.claude/skills/
  ```

On your machine, `~/.claude/skills/pr-connect` and `~/.claude/skills/pr-summ` link to `~/Developer/PRagent/skills/`, so your edits take effect without a reinstall. The skills appear in a new Claude Code session; in this one they're already listed.

content.text:
It's three layers: Claude Code finds the skills, Claude follows each skill's instructions, and small shell scripts fetch the data.

## 1. Claude Code finds the skills

```
~/.claude/skills/
├── pr-connect → ~/Developer/PRagent/skills/pr-connect   (symlink)
└── pr-summ    → ~/Developer/PRagent/skills/pr-summ      (symlink)
```

- When a session starts, Claude Code scans `~/.claude/skills/` and reads the header at the top of each `SKILL.md`:
  ```yaml
  name: pr-summ                 # becomes the /pr-summ command
  description: Fetch a PR...    # lets Claude trigger it from plain words too
  allowed-tools: Bash(bash *fetch_pr.sh*)   # can run the script without a permission prompt
  ```
- Claude only sees the name and description up front. The rest of the file loads when the skill is used.

## 2. You type `/pr-summ 42`

1. Claude Code loads the full `SKILL.md` and replaces `$ARGUMENTS` with `42`. It also fills `${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}` with the skill's folder path.
2. Claude follows the steps written there; they're plain instructions, not code.
3. Claude runs `bash fetch_pr.sh 42`.

## 3. `fetch_pr.sh` gets the data

```
git remote get-url upstream || origin
        │
        ▼
 [redacted]:acme/shop.git   ──sed──►  acme/shop   (the slug)
        │
   ┌────┴─────────────┐
 github.com        bitbucket.org
   │                  │
 gh pr view 42      curl api.bitbucket.org/2.0/repositories/acme/shop/pullrequests/42
 -R acme/shop         + /commits + /diffstat
   │                  │
   └──────► jq ◄──────┘
            │
            ▼
  one JSON shape: {host, repo, number, title, description, author,
                   source, target, state, url, commits[], files[]}
```

- **Why only this project's PRs come back:** every API call includes the slug taken from your current folder's remote. It can't ask for any other repo.
- **Searching by description:** for something like `"login fix"`, it searches titles first (`gh pr list --search` or Bitbucket `q=title ~ "login fix"`).
  - One match: it continues with that PR's number.
  - 0 or several matches: it returns `{"matches":[...]}`, and Claude asks you which one.
- **Same output for both hosts:** `jq` reshapes GitHub and Bitbucket responses into the same JSON fields. Because of that, Claude and the template don't need to know which host the PR came from.

## 4. Claude writes the summary

- Claude reads `template.md`:
  - Fields like `{{title}}` and `{{author}}` are copied from the JSON.
  - Each `<!-- comment -->` is an instruction for Claude to write that section from the PR data.
- The script handles the facts; Claude handles the wording. The skill tells Claude to use only what the PR says and never invent anything.
- The summary is saved to `pr-summaries/github-PR-42.md` and shown in the chat.

## 5. `/pr-connect` works the same way, with `connect.sh`

| Check | GitHub | Bitbucket |
|---|---|---|
| Logged in? | `gh auth status` | email and token in the shell environment, or in `~/.config/pr-agent/bitbucket.env` |
| Not logged in | prints `NOT_CONNECTED` and says to run `gh auth login` | prints `NOT_CONNECTED` and says to run the setup in your own terminal |
| Can read this repo? | `gh repo view acme/shop` | `curl .../acme/shop/pullrequests?pagelen=1` |
| Result | `OK:` or `NO_ACCESS` | `OK:` or `NO_ACCESS` |

- The script prints a short keyword (`OK`, `NOT_CONNECTED` or `NO_ACCESS`), and `SKILL.md` tells Claude what to say for each one.
- `fetch_pr.sh` reads the same Bitbucket file, so once you've connected, `/pr-summ` just works.

## What each file controls

| To change… | Edit |
|---|---|
| The summary format | `skills/pr-summ/template.md` |
| What Claude does | `SKILL.md` |
| How data is fetched | `fetch_pr.sh` or `connect.sh` |

Edits go live in your next Claude session. Push them, and teammates get the changes when they run `git -C ~/.claude/pr-agent pull`.
